name: toot mounds

attributes.attribute: round breast-shaped hills of the English countryside
some carry cairns that form nipples

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Toot mounds are round hills found in the English countryside. The name may come from an Indo-European word meaning to stick out, the root of the words tit and teat. Because of the breast shape, some hills carried cairns placed on top to form nipples. This reinforced the belief that the earth was a womanly, maternal body. The most famous of these hills are in Ireland, where they are known as the Paps of Danu.

okr.objective: Record the British hills called toot mounds.
